newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK banks run out of Beijing Enterprises IPO forms.
newsitem.headline: HK banks run out of Beijing Enterprises IPO forms.

text.p: Hong Kong banks have already run out of a new supply of application forms for Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's initial public offering (IPO), a source close to the underwriters said on Wednesday.

An initial 400,000 application forms were scooped up by potential investors on the first subscription day on Tuesday. A further 500,000 were printed overnight and distributed to underwriters and banks, but they did not last long.
"Banks have run out," the source said.
Peregrine Capital Ltd, one of the global coordinators of the issue, has asked for another 200,000 forms to be printed, a spokesman said.

"There is a legal obligation that there has to be enough forms and we have already ordered another 200,000. That will bring the total to over one million forms," said Tom Grimmer, director for corporate communications at Peregrine Investments Holdings.
Friday is the deadline for applications. The Hong Kong offering is expected to be more than 1,000 times subscribed, the highest ever in the territory.
Beijing Enterprises, which is controlled by the Beijing municipal government, is offering 150 million shares in a global flotation at HK$12.48 per share.
Ten percent of the issue is being offered to the Hong Kong public and 90 percent to international investors.
